Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Board and Management oversight failed: the concept was flawed, controls were inadequate and poorly implemented, Audit Committee reviews were cursory, and the Board was denied information but also did not appreciate what it got.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Both Fastow and Kopper were on the November 5, 1997 call and both had an obligation to disclose Kopper's role. No director except possibly Skilling knew of the Chewco buyback or tax payment. No director had a financial interest in the partnerships.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The Board resolution names Lay and Skilling to approve any changes to Rhythms terms. Later changes (new options, note raised from $50M to $64M) were not presented to them.
Direct_Quote: in the event of a change in the terms of [the Rhythms] transaction from those presented to the Board for its consideration

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The LJM2 presentation said only that 'LJM2 has typical private equity fund fees and promote' targeting '$200 + million institutional private equity,' without compensation detail.
Direct_Quote: LJM2 has typical private equity fund fees and promote

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Andersen flags related-party transactions as an area to be given 'high priorit[y] due to the inherent risks.' Its May 2, 2000 engagement letter covers an examination of management's internal-control assertion as of Dec 31, 2000.
Direct_Quote: high priorit[y] due to the inherent risks that were present

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Considering LJM3, Fastow tells directors additional controls are in place: he still owes fiduciary duties, he can be asked to resign from LJM, Skilling approves all deals, Legal keeps files, and Skilling reviews his economic interest. Directors add quarterly Finance Committee review and Compensation Committee review of Fastow's LJM pay.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The committees are told of further controls: LJM Deal Approval Sheets, an LJM Approval Process Checklist with Skilling review, that LJM professionals never negotiate for Enron, and that Enron negotiators report to people other than Fastow.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The Board authorized Raptor I in May 2000 and could have identified flaws. Raptor III and the restructuring were never brought to the Board, and the February 2001 list mentioned 'Raptors I, II, III, IV' ambiguously.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Causey's annual LJM lists were incomplete: the 1999 list showed 8 of 10 transactions, and the 2000 list omitted buybacks.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Fastow tells the Finance Committee that LJM2's projected IRR is 17.95%. On Oct 26, 2000 he tells LJM2 limited partners 51%, and he never corrects the Committee.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: At the February 2001 reviews, the committees are not told that two Raptors owed Enron ~$175M more than they could pay (in daily reports to Causey and Buy), nor later that the gap reached ~$500M by March, nor about the March 26 restructuring and ~$800M stock transfer.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Actor(s): Arthur Andersen partners (incl. David B. Duncan, Thomas H. Bauer)
Description: Andersen meets internally about serious concerns over Enron's LJM accounting and oversight and reportedly decides to suggest a special Board committee or competitive bidding.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Actor(s): David B. Duncan; Thomas H. Bauer (Andersen)
Description: A week later, in a session including an executive session without management, Duncan reports 'no material weaknesses had been identified' and that Andersen's '[o]pinion regarding internal control ... [w]ill be unqualified.' Neither raises the concerns discussed internally.
Direct_Quote: no material weaknesses had been identified ... [o]pinion regarding internal control ... [w]ill be unqualified.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Committee reviews reportedly lasted 10 to 15 minutes, with no discussion of economic terms or benefits to LJM or Fastow and no probing of Causey's statement that 'the process was working effectively.'
Direct_Quote: the process was working effectively

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Fastow tells the Finance Committee he spends about three hours per week on LJM matters and that LJM deals provided $229.5M of 1999 earnings (vs. $549M net income for those two quarters).

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: K-1s show Fastow's partnership capital up $15M (1999) and $16M (2000), over $31M total, plus $18.7M in distributions in 2000. The Board's review never occurs until October 2001.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Fastow says Skilling received 'a review of [Fastow's] economic interest in [Enron] and the LJM funds.' The Committee unanimously asks the Compensation Committee to review, but it never does. Skilling says he saw only a handwritten Fastow document showing a larger Enron stake.
Direct_Quote: a review of [Fastow's] economic interest in [Enron] and the LJM funds

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Since at least 13 Enron–LJM2 deals had Enron negotiators reporting to Fastow, McMahon complains to Skilling in March 2000. The Committee concludes that 'no one was minding the store.'
Direct_Quote: In short, no one was minding the store.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: McMahon's contemporaneous talking points read: 'LJM situation where AF wears 2 hats and upside comp is so great creates a conflict I am right in the middle of'; 'I find myself negotiating with Andy [to whom he then reported] on Enron matters and am pressured to do a deal that I do not believe is in the best interests of the shareholders'; 'Bonuses do get affected — MK, JM.' He also raised Fastow pressuring banks to invest in LJM2. Skilling recalls only a compensation discussion and takes no action, and McMahon soon transfers away from LJM.
Direct_Quote: I find myself negotiating with Andy [to whom he then reported] on Enron matters and am pressured to do a deal that I do not believe is in the best interests of the shareholders.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Trushar Patel, responsible for later Raptors, is married to Anne Yaeger Patel, who assisted Fastow at LJM2. She and Glisan shared in Southampton while the Raptors were in progress.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Neither set a procedure to capture all LJM deals, and some buybacks never reached them. Causey saw his role as checking sign-offs and Buy as evaluating risk. Buy knew of the Q1 2001 Raptor changes but did not review them.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Fastow tells the Finance Committee that 'Buy, Causey and Skilling review all transactions between the Company and the LJM funds.' Skilling says he may not have been present, signed few approval sheets, and signed only when Causey and Buy had.
Direct_Quote: Buy, Causey and Skilling review all transactions between the Company and the LJM funds.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Some approval sheets are missing or unsigned, have pre-printed check marks, or were completed after closing. They contain boilerplate questions ('Was this transaction done strictly on an arm's-length basis?') and set no requirement to seek third-party buyers, making them 'a formality.'
Direct_Quote: Was this transaction done strictly on an arm's-length basis?
Notes: The S005 EEX approval sheet is an example of this form.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The controls failed structurally: Raptors moved risk 'from one Enron pocket to another,' and in some sales 'it is not clear that anything was really being bought or sold.'
Direct_Quote: it is not clear that anything was really being bought or sold.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Enron announces Skilling's unexpected resignation.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Watkins sends Lay a one-page anonymous letter: 'Enron has been very aggressive in its accounting—most notably the Raptor transactions' and 'I am incredibly nervous that we will implode in a wave of accounting scandals.' Lay viewed it as thoughtfully written. Watkins (ex-Andersen, joined Enron Oct 1993) declined Committee interviews.
Direct_Quote: I am incredibly nervous that we will implode in a wave of accounting scandals.
Notes: Same memo as source S041.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record

Description: Lay and Derrick choose V&E for a 'preliminary investigation' despite its involvement in Raptor and LJM deals. Its scope excludes second-guessing Andersen's accounting or a detailed review of the transactions.
Direct_Quote: preliminary investigation

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Watkins orally tells a friend in Andersen's Houston office about her concerns.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Watkins meets Lay for about an hour with an expanded letter and documents, focused on Raptor. Lay believes she is sincere and promises an investigation.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Other_Parties_or_Subject: Eight Enron officers; two Andersen partners; Watkins (Sept 10); Fastow; Causey
Description: V&E reviews documents, mostly from Global Finance's GC, interviews eight officers and two Andersen partners, and interviews Watkins on Sept 10.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Other_Parties_or_Subject: Kenneth Lay; James Derrick; Robert Jaedicke (Audit Committee Chair)
Description: V&E presents its findings orally to Lay and Derrick, then briefs Jaedicke and, in early October, the full Audit Committee.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: V&E's letter finds procedures 'generally adhered to' and that no one 'could identify any transaction ... that was not reasonable from Enron's standpoint.' It says the accounting is 'creative and aggressive, but no one has reason to believe that it is inappropriate,' recommends no further independent investigation, and warns of 'bad cosmetics' and 'a serious risk of adverse publicity and litigation.'
Direct_Quote: the accounting treatment on the Condor/Whitewing and Raptor transactions is creative and aggressive, but no one has reason to believe that it is inappropriate from a technical standpoint.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record

Direct_Quote: The result of the V&E review was largely predetermined by the scope and nature of the investigation

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record

Description: Enron failed to disclose facts important to understanding the related-party deals, including Fastow's benefits and the purposes, and asserted arm's-length comparability without foundation.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The Big Five petition the SEC for disclosure guidance, including on transactions 'on terms that would not be available from clearly independent third parties.'

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The SEC urges companies to describe related-party transactions' business purpose, economic substance, financial effects and risks.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Actor(s): Enron Financial Reporting Group; Rex Rogers (Assoc. GC); Enron Global Finance; V&E; Andersen; Richard Causey (final arbiter)
Description: Footnotes were drafted by Financial Reporting and circulated widely, with Causey resolving disputes, signing the 10-Q/10-K and deferring to Global Finance. Skilling reviewed the filings, and all directors and Fastow signed the 10-Ks.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Actor(s): Rex Rogers; Vinson & Elkins; James Derrick
Description: Proxy related-party disclosures were organized by Rogers with V&E. Derrick checked only for obvious errors, there was no systematic procedure to identify all related-party transactions, and directors focused on disclosures about themselves.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The May 2000 proxy describes LJM1 and LJM2 as private investment companies, names Fastow as managing member of the GP, and says he gets profits above his capital share, without giving any amount.
Direct_Quote: Andrew S. Fastow, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Enron, is the managing member of LJM1's general partner.

Description: The 2000 proxy discloses eight 2H 1999 transactions ($119.3M for six, $12.9M equity plus a $19.6M loan, and LJM2 borrowing $38.5M) and states the terms were 'reasonable and no less favorable' and 'negotiated on an arm's-length basis with senior officers of Enron other than Mr. Fastow.'
Direct_Quote: negotiated on an arm's-length basis with senior officers of Enron other than Mr. Fastow.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The 2001 proxy discloses 11 transactions ($213M), $76M of sales back to Enron, $127M of LJM2 equity in four vehicles and $2.1B of derivatives notional. It omits that the $76M were buybacks and that $82M had been distributed to LJM2 from Raptors I and II.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record

Description: Fastow avoids answering the proxy questionnaire on his LJM interests, attaching addenda that refer readers to the Global Finance GC (2000) or to prior proxy disclosures (2001). No one presses him for the amount.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: 10-Q/10-K footnotes describe 'a senior officer of Enron' (never naming Fastow) and, from Q2 2000, an unnamed 'Related Party.' Q2 2001 says the officer sold all his interests as of July 31, 2001.
Direct_Quote: [a] senior officer of Enron is managing member of LJM's general partner.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The 10-Qs state that 'all transactions with the Related Party are approved by Enron's senior risk officers as well as reviewed annually by the Board.'

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Filings disclose ~$60M (Q3) and ~$500M (FY 2000) of revenue from Raptor derivatives offsetting merchant losses.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The arm's-length wording shifts from 'reasonable and no less favorable' (Q2-Q3 1999) to 'representative of' (1999 10-K) to 'reasonable compared to' (2000 10-K). Draft notes read 'need positive evidence' and 'needs research,' and no substantiation steps are found.

Description: The 2000 10-K says Enron paid '$123 million to purchase share-settled options ... on 21.7 million shares' without saying they were puts on its own stock. Buybacks are never disclosed.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The 10-Q says the officer sold his interest but not that the buyer was Kopper. V&E recommended disclosing this, but Investor Relations objected.

Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: The partnerships were not 'secret,' but there was 'a strong predisposition ... to minimize the disclosures.' Fastow did not want his compensation disclosed, and some deals (Chewco, Yosemite) were structured to avoid disclosure. Source_Title: Powers Report (Enron board special investigation), House hearing record
Description: Berardino cites the Dec 31, 2001 Big 5 petition (endorsed by AICPA) on MD&A guidance and the SEC's Jan 22, 2002 interpretive release.
